correctness.rationale: A labeled site is one unordered nonloop pair, so sum s_ij=m and s_ij^2=s_ij+2 binom(s_ij,2). Expansion gives QC=9Q-5m+2B. A multiplicity profile has exactly m!/prod s_ij! labeled realizations; multiplying the edge factors and taking degree 3 at every species encodes exactly those weights and u^B, giving the PGF after normalization. The sum of margins gives m=3n/2, with the smallest positive admissible n=2; its only matrix gives an inclusive tail of 1. For n=4, subtracting sums of degrees of opposite vertex pairs forces equality of the corresponding opposite edge multiplicities. Thus there are three nonnegative multiplicities summing to 3, with types (1,1,1), (2,1,0), and (3,0,0). Permuting the types and assigning distinct site labels gives 720, 1080, and 60 matrices with B=0,2,6 respectively. As C=4+B/3, only the maximum gives a strict 5% upper-tail result (60/1860=1/31). The argument is exact for the stated labeled uniform margins; the frozen code and certificate were inspected and agree with the hand derivation at the critical size, not used as proof of the all-size law.

evidence: Greenhill–McKay gives asymptotic enumeration for allowed edge multiplicities and uses factorial weights for pairing counts. Tishby et al. treats cycle counts of degree-two regular graphs, explicitly not degree >=3. A lawful full-text attempt for Artzy-Randrup–Stone did not yield the text.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Allowed-multiplicity asymptotics and the pairing weight do not provide the exact finite collision distribution or threshold. Degree-two components and their cycle laws do not specialize to cubic species graphs. Prior work on sampling a null also would not by itself give this exact law.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Knowing an allowed-multiplicity count, or first two moments under another ensemble, does not yield the entire distribution of summed pair collisions for a uniformly labeled fixed-margin matrix, or the exact mass 1/31 at the top. The coefficient extraction uses a standard mechanism, but the statistical identification and exact calibration require the matched weights and counting the actual critical profiles.

evidence: With column sum two, each site is a labeled edge of a loopless cubic multigraph. B counts unordered pairs of parallel edges (equivalently 4-cycles of the bipartite incidence graph), and identical vertex-labeled multigraph profiles do not all have equal probability.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A genuine equivalent graph law must weight each multiplicity profile by 1/prod s_ij! before normalization and mark each binom(s_ij,2). A uniform census of unlabeled sites or graphs does not generate this distribution.

value.rationale: The complete conditional law is relevant to a named co-occurrence statistic when exact tails matter in small designs. The natural first nondegenerate cubic paired-site design already allows strict rejection, with a verified attainable p-value, whereas the only smaller design never does. This is a concrete resolution limit and a check for fixed-margin null calculations, not an arbitrary table entry or a claim of ecological causation or power.
